note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English; the alate is based only on a queen, and the original states that the colour may be faded. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparisons with all the other species except A. tranquillus have already been made. A. tranquillus is distinguished in both the alate and the worker by the shorter apical tooth and the longer outer margin of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible; in the alate it additionally has the third apical spur of the fore tibia reduced, and in the worker a distinctive enteric valve.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow; pilosity sparse, yellow. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.27. Mandibular apical tooth rather long, L4/Li 0.74, Ra/Ri 0.93; in surface view the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/Li·Lm 14.41; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin slightly shorter than that of the second marginal tooth, Ra/Rj·Rm 14.80. Fore tibia scarcely inflated, Ti/Tw 5.05; third apical spur short, about one quarter the length of the other two spurs. The midgut–hindgut junction is distinctly longer than diagonal; the enteric valve is almost sessile, attached to the second hindgut pouch, dorsolateral in the unopened abdomen; cushion 1 is sclerotized along its whole length, half of it projecting beyond the tips of the spines of the other positions, the margin of the swollen end bearing 25–28 slender spines (mean 26.7), small spines scattered on the outer half of the stalk and on the concave surface of the swollen end, the base of the stalk with transverse wrinkles; the cushions of the other positions bear 3–8 slender, slightly curved spines (mean 5.3), hooked at the tip but not fully reflexed, with smaller spines over the rest of their length; no distinct minute spines were seen on the valve membrane between or outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle roughly circular with a tendency to triangular, slightly concave, smaller than half the ocellus, yellowish brown; central spot circular, flat, slightly smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus chestnut brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark distinct, smooth, semicircular, slightly concave, concolorous with the head capsule; antennae brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum chestnut brown, a dark transverse suture present, weak on the mesonotum; femora brown, tibiae yellowish brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsal spiracles distinct, dark sepia brown, sternites brown with a pale brown median part, ventral spiracles sepia brown; cerci yellowish brown. Posterior margin of head capsule not very evenly rounded, slightly undulate; ocelli moderate, their distance from the compound eye distinctly greater than their minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.23, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture weak. Mandibular apical tooth rather short, L/L1 0.66, Ra/Rj 1.01; in surface view the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/Li·Lm 7.40–9.10; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth equal to or slightly shorter than that of the second. Meso- and metanotum rather narrow at the constriction, M/W 0.26. Cephalic pilosity slightly uneven, with outstanding setae.
